dossier.scp_unleashed.143.title: The Bladewood Grove
dossier.scp_unleashed.143.caption: SCP-143 as first surveyed: one tree, alone on a low rise in open grassland.

page.title: Special Containment Procedures:
text: SCP-143 cannot be moved. A wide fence is to be kept around it, well beyond the reach of its branches, and the ground beneath its canopy is to be treated as a no-entry zone. %rThe wind reaches further.%r
Harvesting is permitted only under a written order. Every branch, plank and cutting taken from SCP-143 is to be logged.
**No cutting of SCP-143 is to be planted outside a secure site.**

page.title: Description:
text: SCP-143 is a single tree resembling a cherry, about fifteen metres tall, with a broad, graceful canopy and near-black bark. Its blossoms are pale pink, almost white, and carry a faint metallic sheen in direct light.

The petals of SCP-143 are as hard and keen as honed steel. They fall continually, drifting on the slightest breeze, and they cut whatever they land on. The cuts they leave are slow to close. More petals fall in wind and rain, and the tree sheds heavily whenever its branches are disturbed. Observers note that petals seem to fall more thickly wherever someone is standing beneath it. %rNo mechanism has been found.%r
Records describe a time when SCP-143 was one of many: whole groves of these trees once grew across open country. Now there is only one.
The wood of SCP-143 is dense, dark and unusually hard. Sawn into planks it behaves much like ordinary timber, though it takes longer to cut.

page.title: Addendum 143-1: Recovery
text: SCP-143 was found standing alone on a low rise, far from any road or settlement, with nothing else growing tall within sight of it. The grass beneath it was matted with fallen petals.
The surveyor who recorded its position did not go closer. %rHis notes end there.%r

page.title: Addendum 143-2: Cuttings
text: Cuttings taken from SCP-143 take root readily and grow into trees of the same kind. Every one has shed petals like its parent.
None of them is the original. %rStaff are asked not to forget which one is.%r

archive.scp_unleashed.notes.scp143.1: You will see it from a long way off.
archive.scp_unleashed.notes.scp143.2: Do not linger under the blossoms.
archive.scp_unleashed.lead.scp143_near: A sweet, cold scent on the wind. Pale petals in the grass.
archive.scp_unleashed.lead.scp143_moved: Field notes updated: the tree stands elsewhere.
jade.scp_unleashed.scp143.original: SCP-143: the last of the grove
jei.scp_unleashed.info.scp143_log.1: Bladewood: dark, dense timber from SCP-143, the last tree of a vanished grove. It saws, burns and builds like any wood, but it takes longer to cut.
jei.scp_unleashed.info.scp143_log.2: Every blow against a living tree shakes its branches. What falls from them is not harmless.
jei.scp_unleashed.info.scp143_leaves.1: Bladewood blossoms shed petals as hard and keen as honed steel. They drift down all the time, and they cut whatever they land on. A petal that misses does nothing at all.
jei.scp_unleashed.info.scp143_leaves.2: More petals fall in wind and rain, and whenever the branches are disturbed. The tree never seems to shed more than when someone stands beneath it.
jei.scp_unleashed.info.scp143_bleeding.1: Bleeding: a petal cut can keep on bleeding for a while afterwards. Fresh cuts make it worse. It passes with time.
jei.scp_unleashed.info.scp143_bleeding.2: People, D-Class, villagers and animals bleed alike.
jei.scp_unleashed.info.scp143_sapling.1: A cutting from SCP-143. Planted on soil in daylight, it grows into another bladewood tree, in time or with bone meal.
jei.scp_unleashed.info.scp143_sapling.2: Trees grown from cuttings shed their petals just like the original.
commands.scp_unleashed.scp143.locate.non: SCP-143 has no site in this world yet. Reading its file chooses one.

commands.scp_unleashed.scp143.place.over: SCP-143 can only be placed in the Overworld.
commands.scp_unleashed.scp143.place.room: There is no room for SCP-143 here.
commands.scp_unleashed.scp143.place.succ: SCP-143 now stands at %s, %s, %s. Any earlier tree is no longer the original.
